The Girl Who Silenced the World – Severn Cullis-Suzuki In 1992, at just **12 years old**, a Canadian girl named **Severn Cullis-Suzuki** traveled to Rio de Janeiro with a group of friends to attend the **United Nations Earth Summit**. They were all part of a small environmental group they had founded called ECO (Environmental Children's Organization). They raised their own money to make the trip. Standing before world leaders, Severn delivered a **remarkable 6-minute speech** that stunned the audience into silence. With calm, clear urgency, she said: > "I’m only a child, and I don’t have all the solutions, but I want you to realize, neither do you. You don’t know how to fix the holes in our ozone layer. You don’t know how to bring back an animal now extinct. And you can’t bring back the forests that once grew where there is now desert. If you don’t know how to fix it, please stop breaking it." Her speech became known as **“The Girl Who Silenced the World for 6 Minutes.”** It went viral before the internet era—broadcast on TV, shared in classrooms, and quoted by activists globally. Though she didn’t become a politician, Severn has continued to work as an environmentalist, author, and speaker. Her speech remains a timeless reminder of the power of youth and truth spoken to power.

My face at the end 🤣🤣 • I don’t even know why I’m posting this crazy stuff other than it’s true to what I did when my 2 aunts and my kids went to the bathroom and left me alone for 5 min by the kids area at the Zoo. • Honestly, I was sleepy after lunch and I needed a jolt of adrenaline…and I LOVE doing stunts…and I saw the hill…and I couldn’t resist. • The roll worked better than a cup of coffee. Better than a soda. Better than candy. • I was re-energized for the next 6 hours of hauling a stroller, 3 kids and one GIANT HEAVY GOLDEN GORILLA (long story) all over the San Diego zoo. 🤣 • No deep message on this post. Just the kind of hijinks I get up to and have never posted or told anyone about because it’s NOT very serious “producer” like behavior. • And I am a SERIOUS person. • But…maybe I’m not? 🤔 • Either way. People seem to enjoy my crazy on the internet. Maybe it’s me or maybe it’s just that people like to watch people fall down. • Because we ALL HAVE FALLEN DOWN before. • It’s very universal: Falling. Falling & failing. • I welcome both. Because both make me get up stronger than I was before. 💪 • This is me following the fun. Finding the joy. I hope this crazy post brings you joy today. Thanks for reading and watching and for re-inspiring me to be myself. Xo Michelle

It's an interesting phenomenon of coincidence, actually; both Liverpool and the Cavaliers played well in the regular season (the former winning the league, the latter beginning with a 15-0 campaign). Yet, both teams seem to falter in the important moments (EFL cup final loss against Newcastle United, R16 loss against PSG, 1-4 loss against the Pacers... the list goes on and on). Join me now too as we recall a familiar team - the Duke Blue Devils, the 1 seed in the 2025 NCAA bracket who ended up falling short to Houston in the semi-finals. On August 23, 2016, the city of Albuquerque, New Mexico, was shaken by the heartbreaking death of 10-year-old Victoria Martens, which happened on the night of her birthday. Her mother, Michelle Martens, had invited her new boyfriend, Fabian Gonzales, and his cousin, Jessica Kelley, into their apartment that evening. Kelley had recently been released from prison, and within hours of their arrival, Victoria was found dead. What followed was a complex and controversial investigation. Michelle initially gave a shocking confession, admitting to letting dangerous individuals around her daughter, but that statement later turned out to be unreliable and contradicted by forensic evidence. Authorities discovered that DNA found at the scene did not match Michelle, Fabian, or Jessica — instead, it belonged to an unidentified man who, even as of 2025, has never been found. Michelle was eventually sentenced to 12 to 15 years in prison for child abuse resulting in death, not for causing harm directly, but for failing to protect her daughter. Fabian was given 37.5 years, and Jessica received 44 years. The case continues to raise serious questions about how the system failed Victoria — and who the unknown fourth person might be. #truecrime #crimestory #truecrimecommunity
